correctness.rationale: Every hypothesis of Xiang (2021) Theorem 2.6 is checked on H=C², K=I/4, Λ_i=Γ_i=the two coordinate functionals, U1=I and U2=coordinate-swap. The pair has exact relative K-lower C=16 and Bessel DΓ=1 (no requirement C≤DΓ since K rescales), each Ui is invertible and commutes with K. The original printed quantity ||U1†|| ||U2−U1|| ||(K*)~⁻¹||=1·2·4=8<16=C/DΓ, but the partition selecting Λ1U1* and Γ2U2* has both coefficients f1 and zero energy at e2 while ||K*e2||²=1/16. The theorem’s conclusion is therefore false as written. The proof’s coefficient-norm triangle inequality demands √C and √DΓ instead of quadratic constants, giving a valid sufficient (not optimal claimed) threshold. Independent matrix arithmetic reconfirmed the precise inequality and failed weave.
